p: Climbing in the middle of west London takes a touch more planning than climbing in a retail park on the edge of a town, mostly because of the travel. Public transport is the easy option round here: Sloane Square on the District and Circle lines is the main Tube for the King's Road, and plenty of buses run along it. Driving and parking in Chelsea can be costly and slow, so leave the car at home if you can.

Book your slot ahead and allow a couple of hours for the full visit. Everyone climbing needs a participation form, with parents or guardians signing for under-18s, and filling it in before you set off saves precious minutes. Check the age guidance too, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers.

Once you're kitted up, start gently. A couple of easy walls first, then the races, then the heart-in-mouth stuff. If somebody's nervous, a low climb and an early let-go shows them just how gently the auto-belay brings you down. Bring water and wear trainers; leave rings and watches behind.

There's lots to pair it with nearby. The Chelsea Physic Garden, one of London's oldest botanic gardens, is a little walled oasis by the river. The National Army Museum, next to the Royal Hospital Chelsea, is free and has plenty for curious kids, and the Royal Hospital's grounds are home to the famous Chelsea Pensioners and the annual flower show.
